newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to reopen schools after meningitis scare.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to reopen schools after meningitis scare.

text.p: The Egyptian government has decided to reopen schools in a south Cairo suburb, closed for the last few days because of a meningitis scare, government newspapers said on Tuesday.
The authorities have sprayed one school from which a 13-year-old boy has died with symptoms of the disease.
Close friends of the family told Reuters on Monday that both the boy, Michael Emile Boulos, and his sister had died but a school official told Reuters on Tuesday his sister was well.
"Only Michael died and his sister is all right," said the official at the school in the luxurious Cairo suburb of Maadi.
"Studies will resume as usual now that the preparatory building has been sprayed," she added.
The authorities have denied the disease is meningitis but they have encouraged parents to vaccinate their children against the disease, which attacks the brain and can quickly kill.
Meningitis usually causes a few deaths at this time of the school year in Egypt.
